name: Polytrope with a random field
blurb: The polytrope (n = 1 by default) threaded by a tangled field with a Kolmogorov spectrum, confined to the star (beta 1000 at its center on average).

featured.label: Mass (M☉)
featured.tip: Mass of the star, in solar masses. With an ideal gas it sets only the physical units the readouts are shown in; an equation of state with physical constants (radiation, degenerate electrons, the tabulated one) takes them from it. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Radius (R☉)
featured.tip: Radius of the star, in solar radii (a white dwarf is about 0.01). With an ideal gas it sets only the physical units the readouts are shown in; an equation of state with physical constants (radiation, degenerate electrons, the tabulated one) takes them from it. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Size (share of the box)
featured.tip: Radius of the star as a share of the box, as the star tool’s Size: how much room is left around it. The star is the same in physical units, on a finer or coarser grid. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Polytropic index n
featured.tip: The star's structure, p = K ρ^(1 + 1/n): the larger n, the more centrally concentrated (3/2 for a convective star, 3 for the Sun's interior). The star is stable against convection only if the gas's adiabatic index is at least 1 + 1/n: n = 1 needs the ideal gas's γ = 2, and a real gas (γ of 5/3 or less) needs n of 3/2 or more. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Plasma beta at the center
featured.tip: Ratio of the gas pressure to the magnetic pressure B^2 / 2 at the star's center: the larger, the weaker the field

featured.label: Random seed
featured.tip: Which random field: each seed gives another
